title: NFL Slate Analyst — Weekly Brief Input
description: Input file consumed by skill/scripts/build_brief.py to render the weekly HTML brief. Narrative fields are the analytical product and cannot be generated from data.

title.description: Brief name shown in the masthead

data_as_of.description: Human-readable timestamp. Required: a brief built Thursday and read Sunday is stale and the reader must know which one they hold.

sample.description: true renders a visible SAMPLE DATA banner. Must be true whenever prices are illustrative rather than retrieved.

beat_close_pct.description: Share of bets that beat the closing line. The primary scorecard.

avg_clv_pts.description: Average closing line value in probability points.

lede.description: 2-4 sentences on the week as a whole: what the market is doing, where the board is soft, the single theme.

markets.description: The by-market-type summary strip. Season CLV split by market reveals where edge actually lives.

read.description: One line on whether this market is currently offering anything.

spread.description: From the HOME team's perspective; negative means home is favored.

narrative.description: 2-4 sentences containing: what the market believes, what the process says, the named disagreement, and the risk. If the disagreement cannot be stated, every market in this game must be a pass.

passed.description: Games examined and skipped entirely. Publishing declines is what makes selectivity verifiable.

book.description: A price without a source is unverifiable.

fair.description: Your fair price in American odds, after devigging.

edge_pct.description: Edge in percentage points vs the NO-VIG price. Below 2% against a sharp price should be reported as no edge.

kill.description: REQUIRED when status is play. What would make this bet wrong, written BEFORE kickoff.

reason.description: REQUIRED when status is pass. One line.
